A.explanation: Four $\beta^-$ decays leave nucleon number at $238$ and raise proton number to $96$, so they cannot give $^{234}_{92}\text{U}$.

B.explanation: $\gamma$-rays carry no charge or nucleon number, so they leave both $238$ and $92$ unchanged.

C.explanation: One $\alpha$-particle reduces the nucleus to $^{234}_{90}$ and two $\beta^-$ particles then raise $Z$ back to $92$, giving $^{234}_{92}\text{U}$.

D.explanation: Two $\alpha$-particles reduce nucleon number to $230$, and eight $\beta^-$ particles raise $Z$ to $96$, giving $^{230}_{96}$ not $^{234}_{92}$.

hints: Notice the nucleon number falls by $238-234=4$ while the proton number stays at $92$ for $^{238}_{92}\text{U}$ to $^{234}_{92}\text{U}$.
Recall that an $\alpha$-particle changes $A$ by $-4$ and $Z$ by $-2$, a $\beta^-$ particle leaves $A$ unchanged and changes $Z$ by $+1$, and a $\gamma$-ray changes neither.
Count how many $\alpha$ emissions are needed for the drop of $4$ in $A$, then work out how many $\beta^-$ emissions are needed to bring $Z$ back up to $92$.
walkthrough: Identify the required changes: $\Delta A = 234-238 = -4$ and $\Delta Z = 92-92 = 0$.
State the decay rules: $\alpha$: $A \to A-4$, $Z \to Z-2$; $\beta^-$: $A$ unchanged, $Z \to Z+1$; $\gamma$: $A$ and $Z$ unchanged.
Only $\alpha$ decay can reduce $A$, so a decrease of $4$ requires one $\alpha$-particle. After one $\alpha$, $^{238}_{92}\text{U} \to ^{234}_{90}\text{Th}$.
The proton number is now $2$ too low at $90$. Each $\beta^-$ adds $+1$ to $Z$ with no change in $A$, so two $\beta^-$ decays give $Z = 90+2 = 92$ while $A$ stays at $234$.
The sequence one $\alpha$ plus two $\beta^-$ therefore gives $^{234}_{92}\text{U}$. This is option C.
